Instrument (EN): Digital Stressors Scale — Turkish revised 41-item healthcare worker version
Question count: 41 final retained items out of original 50
Scales / measured domains (EN): 10 revised factors: ICT Complexity; Work–Life Conflict; Job Insecurity; Data Security Concern; Digital Overload; Cybersecurity Anxiety; Digital Social Pressure; Lack of Technical Support; Low Usability; Technological Unreliability.
Research provenance: Karabulut Meral K, Filiz E, Kıraç R. BMC Digital Health 2026-10-13 DOI 10.1186/s44247-026-00307-3. Turkish healthcare professionals N605. Original 50-item/10-factor DSS reduced to 41 and 10 factors. Same sample for EFA/CFA, 64.01% variance, RMSEA .058 SRMR .051; alpha total .938, domains .712-.852; insufficient AVE (<.5) for some factors; independent replication pending.
DB locales: NOT registered in current live 149 published assessment keys/234 locale versions. This is research metadata, not a runnable DB form.

ES form: No tested Spanish respondent edition evidenced.
Other translations: TR-TR culturally adapted and empirically examined 41-item respondent version N605; new translated REVISED form, not the original 50-item wording; no other validated translations verified.
Target population: Health-sector staff in Türkiye, self-report workplace digitization distress; not general-population or diagnostic norms.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Original DSS copyright owner, Turkish adaptation author and commercial online test-item/translation/scoring redistribution permissions NOT independently cleared; open article access does not authorize commercial questionnaire SaaS use.

Instrument (EN): Stress Resilience Item Bank 10-Item Short Form — Turkish clinical adaptation
Scales / measured domains (EN): Turkish factor1 Self-Confidence and Resilience (7 items: 1,3,4,6,7,8,9); factor2 Difficulty and Deficiency in Emotion Control (3 items: 2,5,10). Original German instrument was unidimensional; Turkish TWO-factor solution is a separate scored structure.
Research provenance: Nural BU et al. BMC Psychology published 2026-07-08 DOI 10.1186/s40359-026-05111-2. 507 DSM-5 mental-factors-affecting-other-medical-conditions clinical participants aged 18-65 + 74 nonclinical controls; total N581. 55 controls retested after 2-4 weeks SAME cohort. EFA two factors, CFA CFI .942 RMSEA .062; alpha total .79, factor1 .78, factor2 ONLY .56; r test-retest .675.
DB locales: Not among 149 current published assessment definition keys or 234 locale versions.
EN form: German original 10-item version distinct; English research article is NOT a validated English respondent edition.
RU form: No validated RU clinical edition verified.
ES form: No validated ES clinical edition verified.
Other translations: TR-TR translation from German with forward/back translation, expert review and pilot N30, empirically studied N581. Original German form is NOT a newly validated Turkish instrument's EN version.
Target population: Adults 18-65: 507 clinically diagnosed patients with mental factors affecting other medical conditions and 74 healthy comparison subjects in Türkiye. Not adolescent/general-population norms.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Study obtained developer permission for research adaptation, NOT commercial digital reproduction/translation/scoring; seek explicit instrument-rights-holder and adaptation author authorization before commercial web use.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / CLINICIAN_ONLY. Factor 2 internal consistency alpha .56 weak; original ONE-factor scoring must NOT be transposed uncritically. Clinical/health-sensitive data and interpretive safeguards required; no digital activation.

Instrument (EN): Work-Life Balance Scale — Swedish 4-item cross-cultural adaptation
Scales / measured domains (EN): One overall subjective work–life balance factor: fit between work and non-work activities; no independently validated subscale scores.
Research provenance: Degerstedt F et al. BMC Psychology 2026-10-09 DOI 10.1186/s40359-026-05752-3. Swedish translation: forward/back translation, cognitive debriefing N8. Of 232 trainees, n215 complete for CFA and reliability (police students 173; correctional/probation trainees 42). One-factor CFA CFI/TLI 1.0, SRMR .01, RMSEA .07; alpha .83, omega .86. Reverse item loading .49 vs others .88-.96; no temporal invariance or test-retest.
DB locales: Not published in the present 149-key, 234-version Supabase assessment inventory.
EN form: Original English four-item work-life-balance instrument exists; NOT an independently validated English translation of this Swedish revision.
RU form: No independently validated Russian respondent form found.
ES form: No independently validated Spanish respondent form found.
Other translations: SV-SE: new Swedish translated/culturally adapted participant questionnaire assessed in N215 complete respondents; not known to be validated for all Swedish occupational populations.
Target population: Swedish police-academy students and prison/probation officer trainees, not representative employed adult workers, ages varied.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Published open-access paper and readable Swedish items do NOT independently establish permission to offer the original or Swedish questionnaire commercially online; rights-holder permission for hosted items, derivatives and scoring still required.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / PERMISSION_REQUIRED. One weak reverse-worded item (.49); ceiling effect 15.8%; no broad population norms, responsiveness or cross-language measurement invariance. No commercial test release.
